mod.name: Crucible Editor Controls
mod.description: The Crucible editor with simpler controls: WASD to move, arrow keys, Ctrl + left drag or the middle button (scroll wheel pressed) to turn the camera, the wheel to zoom, Ctrl + right click to delete what is under the cursor, hold the right button to hide the held piece so nothing is placed. Shift + middle drag or Z/C orbit, Q/E and Alt + wheel rotate the piece being placed (Shift + wheel, or Shift + Q/E, rotates it by 5 degrees), Page Up/Down raise and lower the whole grid, Ctrl + Up/Down raise and lower the selected object. A Wire tool (tool bar, after Notes) wires anything that sends a signal (switches, plates, handling markers, triggers, areas) to anything with a tag (doors, traps, tiles ...), read from the configurations by what they are made of, one connection at a time; Pick in the scene lights up what can be wired to; striped rays join them; it makes and removes the handling markers it needs. An Errors tool (tool bar, after the eraser) lists the validation errors with Move Camera buttons that go to and mark the place in red. A Tools menu (next to Controls) chooses which tools the tool bar shows and in what order (by default Select, Region, Move, Copy, Wire, Tiles, Ground, Wall, Place, Areas, Globals, Eraser, Errors and Find). What is selected is counted in the menu bar. More tools, every tool has a collapsible explanation: Find (search the scene by name, tag, signal or place; go to or select the results), Tags (every tag, who has it and who signals it; the ones that lead nowhere; rename a tag everywhere), Lint (more checks than the validation: signals to nowhere, stacked props, empty shapes), Stats (what the scene holds), Marks (camera bookmarks, kept in the scene's notes), Measure (the distance between two clicked points) and Replace (give everything that uses one configuration another). The config editors get a Path button (hidden until View > Path Buttons is ticked) on every property (copies its path, for Direct parameters). The Controls menu (next to File, Edit, View) assigns every control, with profiles: Legacy and Modern (the editor's own two schemes, which replace its modern-controls checkbox), New (these) and your own.
